question: A man reduces his speed from 20 kmph to 18 kmph. So, he takes 8 minutes more than the normal time. What is the distance traveled by him?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio = 20 : 18 = 10 : 9

Time ratio = 9 : 10 (since Distance is constant)

Difference in time ratio = 1 unit = 8 minutes.

Normal time (9 units) = 9 × 8 = 72 minutes = 72 / 60 hours.

Distance = Normal Speed × Normal Time = 20 × (72 / 60) = 24 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Normal Speed (S₁) = 20 kmph

Reduced Speed (S₂) = 18 kmph

Difference in time (ΔT) = 8 minutes = 8 / 60 hours = 2 / 15 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance (D) = (S₁ × S₂) / (S₁ − S₂) × ΔT

 
• 
 
 
 
 
 Start
 End
 
 Distance (D) = ?
 
 

 Speed: 20 kmph | Time: T
 
 

 Speed: 18 kmph | Time: T + 8 min

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the required distance be D km.

⇒ Time taken at 18 kmph = D / 18 hours

⇒ Time taken at 20 kmph = D / 20 hours

⇒ According to the question, the difference in time is 8 minutes.

⇒ D / 18 − D / 20 = 2 / 15

⇒ (10D − 9D) / 180 = 2 / 15

⇒ D / 180 = 2 / 15

⇒ D = (2 × 180) / 15

⇒ D = 360 / 15

⇒ D = 24 km

**∴ The correct answer is 24 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. When they move in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Average Speed

If equal distances are covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) / (S₁ + S₂).

Distance Formula with Time Difference

If a person travels a distance at speed S₁ and S₂ with a time difference ΔT, the distance can be calculated directly using: Distance = (S₁ × S₂) / (S₁ − S₂) × ΔT.
